findings.desc: packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:1706 treats providerLaunchState=granted with providerIdentity=null and a dead workerPid as replacementSafe=true. A real crash window exists between the detached child spawn at packages/main/src/core/host-run.ts:1228 and durable onSpawn identity publication at :1319; killing the worker there can leave the provider process group alive but untracked. Deadline or cancel reconciliation can then publish a supposedly safe terminal and authorize a duplicate replacement while the original provider can still write results.

packages/main/src/handlers/host-run.ts:332 exposes the durable runId before blocking only for --detach; foreground mode waits for terminal at :522 and returns runId only at :573. If the attaching caller disconnects or is terminated before terminal, a replacement caller has no supported run identity or listing command for host_run_status. The caller-loss E2E bypasses the public contract by writing runId from an injected launcher at packages/main/src/tasks/managed-host-run-e2e-smoke.ts:109, leaving foreground caller-loss reattachment and duplicate-retry prevention unimplemented.

packages/main/src/handlers/managed-review-evidence.ts:256 and :313 seal the immutable run-side evidence binding before persisting the ReviewPass or Findings at :267 and :324. A failure before story evidence persistence leaves a binding with no imported evidence. Retry misses the existing-evidence recovery path, creates a new importedAt at packages/main/src/core/managed-review-evidence.ts:378, and is rejected as a different immutable binding by packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:2048. The existing crash test injects failure only after persistence, so an authentic receipt can be permanently stranded instead of converging idempotently.

packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:1124 returns immediately after the claim timeout when claim.json merely exists, although the worker writes that claim at :1156 before potentially slow one-shot input reads and does not transition the snapshot to running until :1192. Therefore detached host_run can truthfully own a worker yet return state=submitted, contradicting the promised claim-handshake result of running; the slow-read smoke at packages/main/src/tasks/managed-host-run-smoke.ts:704 asserts only that the returned state is not failed.

packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:1659 performs next-touch TERM/KILL cleanup but returns only a boolean. Reconciliation then calls writeTerminal with result=null, whose fallback at :878 records termSent=false and killSent=false whenever cleanup succeeded. Timeout and cancellation receipts can therefore report cleanup facts contradicted by the signals actually sent, violating the operator-facing exact cleanup contract even when replacementSafe is correct.

packages/main/src/handlers/host-run.ts:318 and :618 do not reproduce the command schemas' integer, finite, positive/nonnegative, and waitMs maximum constraints. Direct handler callers can supply fractions, infinities, negatives, or waitMs above 30000; downstream boundedPositiveMs silently defaults, floors, or clamps them instead of rejecting them. This violates the repository's mandatory runtime revalidation rule for every Zod constraint and makes handler behavior differ by dispatch path.

packages/main/src/core/provider-process-registry.ts:335 suppresses both registry-lock and slot-unlink failures during release, while packages/main/src/core/managed-host-run.ts:527 suppresses git worktree removal failure and then deletes the filesystem directory. These mutation failures are neither thrown nor recorded as health diagnostics, so operators can receive false concurrency refusals or retain stale Git worktree registrations without an observable cause, contrary to the repository MUTATION fail-fast policy.

readManifest.scanEscalationReason: Candidate routing reported candidate_cutoff_tie and missing protected managed-run and managed-review sources, so the review expanded to the durable lifecycle, evidence importer, shared admission boundary, command handlers, and focused adversarial tests.
